title: Card mode: the hand
summary: Six one-use cards live under your strip, folded to one line, and open in two rows of three when you want them. When the other side plays a card, it turns face up once, then its effect plays on the board.
problem: Card mode adds a hand of six cards to a full chess board. A hand that is always open takes room from the board and makes small text hard to read. A hand that hides its cards hides the main part of the mode.
idea: Fold the hand to one line, 'Cards · 6', under your strip. A tap opens two rows of three named cards. A card reads like a piece: the same reading card. Use marks its targets on the board. Their card turns face up once, before its effect, so the cause is always clear.

borrows.what: The reveal: a card turns face up, then its effect plays. In King Down the cause shows before the effect on the board.
The hand at the edge that fans up on your turn (option B), and the readable card focus.
A coin by the king for each card (option C).
The rule is in view before you act: each card says if it uses your turn or comes before your move.

options.name: Folded hand
options.summary: One line, 'Cards · 6', under your strip. A tap opens two rows of three named cards.

options.name: Hand at the edge
options.summary: Card tops rest at the lower edge on their turn and fan up on your turn, as in Hearthstone and Marvel Snap. The card text is small.

options.name: Coins by the king
options.summary: Each card is a round coin beside your king. It uses no extra row, but the names hide.

recommendation: Pick A. The board keeps its full size, every card shows its name and its state in words when open, and a player who wants only to move never sees more than one line.
notes: Proposed hand only. The deal of six cards is an open owner question (TASKS.md, Card deal). These six are a sample. The lab deals the same random six to both sides.
The cards are real engine cards: Freeze, Strike, Haste, Flight, Rally and Rage. The engine checks every target. Rage has a quiet gold edge and the word Rare. Its legendary look waits for the owner.

One strong moment: their card. In 'their-card', the count in their strip turns to the card's face, the card shows over the turn line, and then the Archer moves. So the check has a visible cause. A tap or a key skips to the end of the reveal.
Your own card stays quiet: a chip lands in your strip, and the turn line shows the second step ('played': two dots and 'Now make your move.').
One card a turn: in 'locked', the other five cards say 'Next turn' in words, and the reading card says why.
Hold a piece (or press I) to read it: the same reading card as a card. Reading never plays a move. A tap on a marked square plays.
On desktop, one context area sits under their strip. You, the hand toggle and the bar stay in one place when the hand opens.
B and C play too. The renders show A in full.
Not shown: the deal moment and the countdown ring (owner question).
Limits: no art exists for cards. Power cards use the king emblems. Rally and Rage use a line icon. Card mode is a lab mode. The computer plays its cards at Casual.
